scenes.visual: Big navy hook text pops word by word; Norb peeks curious from below.
scenes.cardText: What if your memories aren't recordings?
scenes.voiceover: What if your memories aren't recordings?

scenes.visual: Navy file drawer; a krem memory card rises up, glows with a mustard halo (editable!), gains a small teal detail, then slides back down. Norb watches, curious.
scenes.voiceover: When you remember something, your brain doesn't press play. It pulls the memory out of storage — and for a few minutes, it goes soft and editable.

scenes.visual: Three memory cards left to right: first is crisp coral (ORIGINAL), second tilted and mustard (RECALLED), third tilted more and teal (DRIFTED). Norb looks exhausted.
scenes.voiceover: While it's open, today's mood and new details quietly leak in. Then it saves again — a little changed. Recall it enough, and it drifts far from what really happened.

scenes.visual: File drawer again; card rises, the teal detail is added deliberately, then re-files calmer. Norb gets the idea.
scenes.voiceover: But that open window is a gift too. Recall a rough memory, add one calmer thought, and your brain re-saves the gentler version.

scenes.visual: THE SCIENCE card; below it a memory card with a padlock — it springs open, card glows EDITABLE (mustard), then the lock snaps shut again. Norb curious.
scenes.cardText:
Recall makes memory editable.
Then it re-stores — changed.
Researchers call it reconsolidation.
scenes.voiceover: Every time you pull up a memory, your brain has to store it all over again. Researchers call it reconsolidation — and that re-save window is where it can change.

scenes.visual: TRY THIS card; below it the drawer opens and a card rises with a fresh teal dot, then re-files. Norb celebrates.
scenes.cardText:
Replay good memories often.
When a hard one surfaces, add one calmer thought.
scenes.voiceover: Replay good memories often — you strengthen them. And when a painful one surfaces, add one calmer thought before it files itself away.
